newsitem.title: GERMANY: Greenpeace in fresh feeds plant protest over soya.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace in fresh feeds plant protest over soya.

text.p: Activists from environmental group Greenpeace absailed from the roof of a German compound feed plant in their latest protest over the use of transgenic soymeal on Friday.
A Greenpeace statement said the activists had hung banners from the roof of a plant operated by Raiffeisen Sued GmbH in Wuerzburg in Bavaria state.
The banners called for an end to the use of genetically modified soybeans in animal feeds.
Greenpeace opposes the use of meal derived from transgenic soybeans and claims a majority of German farmers in a survey rejected the use of feeds containing genetically modified raw materials.
Greenpeace press officer Svenja Koch said by telephone from Wuerzburg the activists had spoken to the plant management but had been told there was no demand for feed free of transgenic soymeal.
She said the group would stay in the region until May 1 to discuss the issue with local farmers and inform them about methods of testing soybeans for transgenic organisms.
The organisation demands the new soybeans should be traded and labelled separately. It says the beans, developed by U.S. chemicals firm Monsanto, may bring unknown health risks.
